outputs.summary: `parseBoard(files)` (src/core/board/parse.ts) is a pure parser for old-style boards. It takes `{path, text}` pairs and returns `{epics, skipped}`. Epics come in three kinds: `epic`, `standalone` or `orphan`. Each has its folder status, source paths, body and criteria, and tickets in `M` order with Markdown bodies and checked state. Collapsed done epics yield one ticket per `### NNN.M` section under `## Sub-tickets`. Bad files are skipped one at a time with a reason, under size, count and length limits. Fenced code is never read for structure. `boardEpicImport(epic)` (plan.ts) maps one epic to `create_epic` input plus `update_plan_draft` ops: one sprint, tickets in order, unchecked criteria only, and a file reference to the source. The intent notes the source path so DM-18 can detect repeats. Dependencies come only from explicit "Depends on" lines and never close a cycle. `readBoard` (src/core/repo/boardFiles.ts) is the thin read-only adapter, which refuses links and paths outside board/.

content.summary: Sprint 1 met its goal. This repository now runs on Dark Mechanicus alone: `board/`, the `complete-ticket` and `collapse-epic` skills and every board instruction are gone, and the delivery standards keep TDD-first and the full gate while tracking work as Dark Mechanicus epics and tickets. The desktop app can write the Claude Code `.mcp.json` from the folder home (role, save setting, confirmation before replacing a different entry) and during onboarding (on by default, never replaces). For the packaged macOS app the generated entry is identical to the hand-written file. A pure board parser and mapping read this repository's historical board from real fixtures and produce `create_epic` plus `update_plan_draft` inputs that the real schemas accept, ready for the sprint 2 import. All four tickets were accepted on their first attempt after the orchestrator merged each into `planning-switchover`, reviewed it, and re-ran the full gate plus `smoke:mcp` on the integrated branch (af289fa). **Decisions needed at this checkpoint:** the sprint 2 entry criterion asks you to approve the `.mcp.json` defaults (planner role, `--allow-save`, `--label "Claude Code"`); also see the open questions in the epic comment and the risks below.

content.summary: Sprint 2 met its goal, and with it the epic. Setting up a repository that has an old-style `/board` now previews its open epics, done epics and skipped files. It imports open epics as Backlog draft plans through a shared core command (`import_board` over MCP), without duplicates on re-run. Then, as a separate confirmed step, it removes the old board files after listing every one; nothing is committed. DM-20 built a packaged macOS app from the integrated branch (0e99dff) and ran the whole setup on a clone of this repository at its last board commit. A fresh Claude Code session in that clone found the generated project server, connected once approved, and listed 37 Dark Mechanicus tools. All three tickets were accepted on their first attempt. DM-19's worker stalled during fireguard and its lease expired while the Mac slept, so the orchestrator restored a leftover mutant, ran fireguard on the integrated branch, and reconciled the attempt as a resubmission. The full gate plus `smoke:mcp` passes on 0e99dff. **Decisions for you:** whether to commit `.mcp.json`, and whether to merge `planning-switchover` (a PR also needs this epic's `.darkmechanicus` records).
